TASK: Memory and spatial cognition.
(1) Working memory: bounded slot buffer (capacity K, e.g. 4/7/9) with chunking/compression of recurring task contexts; effect on routing in worlds with RECURRING task contexts (build a workload generator with recurring contexts in your bin, plus use sim.rs scenarios). Measure routing success vs fair baselines (see common brief), vs no-buffer, vs unbounded buffer; include a control with no recurrence.
(2) Persistent on-disk shared memory store ("shared memory folder"): append-only log + index (flat and/or HNSW from memory.rs, or memory-mapped if possible without new dependencies) with fast retrieval; measure latency (p50/p99), recall@k vs exact, bytes on disk, and warm-open time vs full reload/rebuild, crash-safety (truncated tail record is recovered), multi-reader sanity. Use std only; no new crates unless audited per the security rule.
(3) Spatial memory: 2D/3D coordinates; k-d tree and uniform grid index; queries: nearest-object, k-NN, range, path length (e.g. Manhattan/A* on a grid), layout overlap (AABB). Property tests against brute force with correctness tests; benchmark speedup vs brute force at several N. Optional "visual-spatial tasks" as task features for the router.
Report HONESTLY whether any of this improves ROUTING outcomes (held-out seeds 31-60, paired CI, Holm) or only speed/memory. Write results/r3_memory_spatial.json. handback.t:
R3 report (memory and spatial cognition). All three parts are built, tested and run. `cargo test --release --lib` passes (165/165). Protocol throughout: tune on seeds 1-8, held-out seeds 31-60, paired 95% t-CI, Holm correction, best fair baseline chosen per world by held-out mean.

**Files (all new, plus 2 lines appended to src/lib.rs):**
- `src/workmem.rs`: contains the working-memory router, the recurring-context workload generator, the store (`workmem::store`), and an evaluation harness (`workmem::harness`).
- `src/spatial.rs`
- `src/bin/r3_workmem.rs`, `r3_store.rs`, `r3_spatial.rs`
- `results/r3_memory_spatial.json`: keys `workmem`, `store`, `spatial`. Each binary merges its own key; console logs are `results/r3_*_output.txt`.
- `results/research_board.md`: R3 section appended.

**Rerun** (from `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh`, release build, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r3`): `cargo run --release --bin r3_workmem` (about 73 s), `r3_store` (about 50 s, `--n 30000` by default), `r3_spatial` (about 70 s).

**Does any of this improve routing? Short answer: working memory does, but only where it is built to; the store and spatial index are speed/robustness only; spatial router features did not help.**

**1. Working memory.** The wrapper keeps K per-context slots of the Hebbian-robust router (LRU eviction, optional label chunking) inside the keyword warm start. K=0 is exactly warm(hebbian-robust), which was the best fair baseline in every recurring world.
- **Recurring worlds** (my generator, explicit context labels; the fair baselines see the label only as a feature, so they cannot represent topic x context):
  - recur-6fam: K>=6 gives +0.061 [+0.050,+0.073], Holm p<1e-4 (0.533 -> 0.594, oracle 0.85). K=4 gives only +0.017 and K=2 about 0, so too few slots thrash.
  - marker present on only 50% of tasks (carry-over of the last context): +0.086 for K>=7.
  - 12 contexts: K=9 +0.023, unbounded +0.036.
  - Chunking, 4 families x 3 variants: K=4 chunked gives +0.078 [+0.064,+0.093]. It also beats the unbounded unchunked buffer by +0.089, because merging variants pools data.
  - The Holm win in more than one world is met (4 of 4 recurring worlds).
- **Where the gain comes from:** having a context-keyed memory, not from the buffer being bounded. A bounded K only matches unbounded when K is at least the number of contexts.
- **Controls where it should not help:**
  - Never-recurring contexts: the buffer hurts, -0.013 to -0.019 vs best fair, Holm p about 1e-4.
  - Contexts that recur but are irrelevant: -0.13 for K>=7, from splitting the data.
  - sim.rs scenarios (context = drift window): fixed scenario shows a K=2 win of +0.030 (Holm p=.0015). I believe the window label leaks the drift time rather than reflecting recurrence. K>=7 loses -0.035 there; the other three scenarios show no win.
- **Verdict:** a conditional win. Don't enable it without evidence that contexts recur and matter, and it needs a guard that falls back to the global router when a slot doesn't beat it. The generator is mine, so this shows the mechanism works, not that real ruflo traffic has recurring contexts.

**2. Persistent store** (`workmem::store`: append-only log, checkpoint snapshot, flat or HNSW index). Std only, no mmap, no new crates. N=30k, dim 128:
- **Latency:** flat exact p50 340 us / p99 525 us. HNSW is only 1.3-2.5x faster at recall@10 of 0.96-0.99 (ef 32-128), with about 11x the memory and an 11 s build.
- **Disk:** 548.6 B per vector, 7.2% over raw f32.
- **Open time:** flat warm open 33 ms vs cold replay 38 ms (1.2x). HNSW warm open 1.4 s vs cold 10.8 s, because the graph is rebuilt in parallel from the snapshot rather than persisted. The OS file cache was warm for these timings.
- **Crash safety:** 150/150 random truncations recovered exactly, and 150/150 single-bit flips were detected at the damaged record (CRC32).
- **Concurrency:** 1 writer and 4 concurrent readers, 0 violations. A second writer is refused via a lock file.
- This is infrastructure; it does not change routing outcomes.

**3. Spatial** (`src/spatial.rs`: k-d tree and uniform grid in 2D/3D; k-NN, nearest, range and radius queries; AABB overlap; A*; layout features).
- **Correctness:** property-tested against brute force, including ties, duplicates, empty and single-point inputs. A* equals BFS on 60 random maps; sweep-and-prune equals the brute-force overlap pairs.
- **Speedup vs brute force:**
  - N=1e5 uniform 2D: k-NN10 about 2800x, nearest about 55x, range about 110x.
  - N=1e6 2D: k-NN10 about 13,000x.
  - N=1e3: nearest only 2-4x.
  - Clustered 3D data with uniform queries: nearest is 0.7x, slower than brute.
  - A* is 2.0-2.5x faster than BFS; AABB sweep is 9x / 20x / 55x at n=500 / 2000 / 8000.
- **Spatial features as router features:** negative for routing. In a world where the best agent depends on the layout class, eps-greedy gains +0.024 [+0.012,+0.037], but hebbian-robust loses -0.022 (Holm p=.004), warm(hebbian) shows no significant change, and pooled-ts shows none. In the control where layout is irrelevant, every learned router loses 0.05-0.10. Additive-feature routers can't use an interaction feature.

**Security:** no packages installed and no dependencies added; hnswlib/faiss were not used.

**Build notes:** the cold first build took about 4.5 min. In edition 2024 `gen` is a reserved word, so the world-generator field is named `mkg` in `r3_workmem.rs`.
